name: Banque Saudi Fransi
legal_name: Banque Saudi Fransi (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: 1977 (Royal Decree M/23 dated 4 Jun 1977; began operations 11 Dec 1977 by taking over the Saudi branches of Banque de l'Indochine et de Suez). CR 1010073368. Rebranded 'BSF' on 4 Jun 2024.
ownership_summary: Listed on the Saudi Exchange; share capital SAR 25bn (2,500m shares). Substantial shareholders at 31 Dec 2025: Kingdom Holding Company 16.199% and Rashed Abdul Rahman Al Rashed & Sons Co. 9.999% (unchanged during 2025). Foreign ownership 15.9% (1H 2026 presentation). Crédit Agricole (former 31.1% holder via CA-CIB) fully divested by 2019.

shareholders.holder: Rashed Abdul Rahman Al Rashed & Sons Co.

government_link: No government entity among substantial (5%+) shareholders at 31 Dec 2025 (AR 2025). One director (Abdulmajid Al Hagbani) is a senior director at the Public Investment Fund per his official bio; the bio does not say he represents PIF.
group_structure: Parent bank with 100% subsidiaries: Saudi Fransi Capital (BSF Capital: brokerage, asset management, corporate finance; profiled separately as sa-bsf-capital), Saudi Fransi for Finance Leasing (JB: Islamic auto leasing and personal finance), Sakan Real Estate Financing, Sur Multi Family Office Limited (UK; wealth management for HNW clients), BSF Markets Limited and BSF Finance Limited (Cayman), plus Saudi Fransi Insurance Agency, Sofinco Saudi Fransi and Saudi Fransi Digital Ventures (all under liquidation). Associate: Banque BEMO Saudi Fransi (Syria). Double counting: BSF Capital is consolidated; its AUM and the 'Investment banking and brokerage' segment appear in both sa-bsf and sa-bsf-capital. Never add them.

footprint: Saudi Arabia: 78 branches, 353 ATMs and 33,787 POS terminals at 30 Jun 2026; private banking centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Alkhobar. Abroad: Sur Multi Family Office Limited (London, UK) and Cayman SPVs; associate in Syria.
customer_segments: Corporate and institutional (about 79% of the loan book), SME/business banking, retail mass market, affluent (Advance, Privilege, Elite, Elite Plus), private banking (HNW), resident expatriates (premium programmes for residents), consumer finance via JB.
business_lines: Corporate banking (45% of H1 2026 operating income), Retail banking (incl. private banking), Treasury (17%), Investment banking and brokerage via BSF Capital (5%). H1 2026 segment operating income (SAR '000): retail 1,799,482; corporate 2,486,763; treasury 972,174; investment banking and brokerage 298,701.

capabilities.wealth_summary: BSF serves wealth clients through its Personal Banking Group (Retail Banking for mass and affluent clients, plus Private Banking) and through its 100% investment arm Saudi Fransi Capital (BSF Capital), which held SAR 34.8bn AUM at 30 Jun 2026. Published affluent tiers are Advance, Privilege, Elite and Elite Plus (Elite Plus: SAR 3m initial deposit or SAR 1.5m six-month average); affluent customers grew 10% in 2025 within 1.36m personal banking customers. Private Banking (centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Alkhobar) relaunched its strategy in early 2025 and aims to be 'the Kingdom's leading private bank' from 2026; the bank also owns Sur Multi Family Office Limited (UK, incorporated Feb 2023) for HNW families. Investment products (funds, discretionary portfolios, brokerage, advisory) are provided by BSF Capital, which expanded its BlackRock partnership in Feb 2025 for globally diversified, Shariah-compliant multi-asset portfolios and planned a mobile 'BSF Invest App' for early 2026. Strategy 2030 (16 Feb 2026) names 'Accelerate Wealth Management in BSFC', 'Upgrade brokerage ecosystem' and 'Differentiation in Affluent' as priorities, while the bank app offers only IPO subscription for investing.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking (within the Personal Banking Group) serves HNW clients with dedicated RMs and centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Alkhobar. Offer per official page: conventional and Islamic banking, term and structured deposits, derivatives/FX/commodities, Lombard-style advances, personal and home finance, offshore tax and estate planning, Shariah-compliant investments and investment solutions through BSF Capital. New PB strategy launched early 2025 with four pillars (products and service excellence incl. project-based financing for HNW project investors and a family programme with netting; client personas; sales acceleration; enablers incl. digital/AI investment tools). Targets leadership in Saudi private banking from 2026. 29 Sep 2026: one-year MoU with Diriyah Company for PB clients (investment packages with luxury real estate, Shariah financing). UK subsidiary Sur Multi Family Office Limited provides wealth management services to BSF's HNW clients and families (BSF loan to it SAR 46m at end-2025). Q2 2026 call: retail personal loan growth included Lombard loans.

asset_management.detail: Through BSF Capital (100%): AUM SAR 34.8bn at 30 Jun 2026 (31.0bn at 31 Dec 2025). Mutual funds (conventional and Shariah-compliant, KSA and international), discretionary portfolios, private placements and public funds. FY2025 FS: funds managed had NAV SAR 30,971m, including Islamic funds of SAR 3,303m. 2025: eight real estate funds initiated (expected development value above SAR 5bn), a Rixos resort fund, a film fund and an industrial city fund. See sa-bsf-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through BSF Capital: local and international share brokerage, custody and margin lending (segment description and PB page). Brokerage trading value SAR 17.8bn in 2Q 2026 and 13.9bn in 1Q 2026. H1 2026 brokerage and asset management fees fell 17% YoY. Strategy 2030 includes 'Upgrade brokerage ecosystem'/'brokerage system upgrade' at BSF Capital. On the Q4 2025 call management said it would 'push for more of our fair share of brokerage and asset management fees'.

digital_investing.detail: Limited in the bank app: the BSF Mobile services list includes IPO subscription and transfers to brokerage companies, but no funds, equities or portfolios. Trading runs on BSF Capital's own channels. BSF Capital planned a 'BSF Invest App' (mobile-first, globally diversified portfolios, later BSF Capital mutual and private funds) for early 2026 (AR 2025); launch not confirmed in sources read. Bank digital KPIs: active digital user rate 72% of registered users and 90% of transactions on mobile (2025); digital penetration of clients 65-70% in 1H 2026 vs 100% target for 2030.

advisory.detail: Investment advisory provided by BSF Capital for Private Banking clients (PB page). In 2025 BSF Capital moved from a product-driven to an advisory-led wealth model and built a specialist internal investment solutions team; Elite and Privilege clients have RMs; the AR reports 'enhanced advisory services for affluent clients'.

discretionary.detail: 'Discretionary portfolio management' listed under BSF Capital asset management on the Private Banking page. No discretionary AUM split disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: AR 2025: through the BlackRock alliance 'clients now have access to investment portfolios which are globally diversified and sharia compliant' (advisory-led), and the planned BSF Invest App will offer diversified investment portfolios. No evidence found that a self-directed robo/model-portfolio app is live as of Oct 2026.

funds_platform.detail: BSF Capital funds plus third-party funds: the PB page says the relationship with BlackRock, Nomura and Ashmore brings their funds and private placements to Saudi investors. No fund-platform technology provider named.

structured_products.detail: Structured deposits for Private Banking and Elite Plus; derivatives, FX and commodities products for PB clients. A revised Derivatives Sales Policy for Corporate and PB clients was adopted (AR 2025). Issuers not named.

private_markets.detail: BSF Capital private placements and real estate/hospitality/film/industrial funds launched in 2025; PB page mentions 'other private placement opportunities'. PB-Diriyah MoU (Sep 2026) for real estate investment packages.

islamic_wealth.detail: Conventional bank with Islamic products under an independent Shariah Board. Shariah-compliant investments for PB; Islamic mutual funds of SAR 3,303m (end-2025); BlackRock portfolios described as Shariah compliant; Shariah-based deposits SAR 66.9bn and Shariah-based loans SAR 165.7bn at 30 Jun 2026.
